reasoning.text: The render reads unambiguously as an FPGA NTT accelerator floorplan: open butterfly-array frame with 8 distinct copper multiplier lanes and symmetric add/sub blocks, 8 interleaved blue BRAM banks with input/output FIFOs on the -X edge, the conflict-free crossbar spine, layered+arrowed read/twiddle/return buses, the exploded radix-4 cutaway, and the raised exploded heatsink that (after last pass) no longer blankets the twiddle ROM, addr-gen or schedule blocks in the TOP plan view. The single remaining render-grounded defect was the shared Barrett reduction spine (mod_red_mult cylinder + mod_red_subshift box) sitting at the same height as the +X pipeline-register column, so in ISO the two reduction members partly merged into the register row; this pass lifts the spine and pulls the register column -X so both reduction members now read distinctly in the X-ray. The only items still imperfect (paper Sec.III bank()/offset() map, per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s, rearranged-loop twiddle addressing, exact FSM table, and the bit-reversed-ROM-vs-natural-order tension) are source-bound: the CFNTT PDF body is FlateDecode-undecodable, so they are correctly labelled [conv]/[source-missing] in the spec and cannot be made paper-faithful inside this visual loop — no achievable scene change is worth >2 points.

fields.before: Pipeline register latching lane-0 outputs before the shared modular-reduction stage.
fields.after: Pipeline register latching lane-0 outputs before the shared modular-reduction stage; pulled -X to open a clear gap to the lifted Barrett reduction spine in the X-ray.

fields.before: First member of the shared modular-reduction stage: a cylindrical Barrett quotient-multiplier spine running the full depth of the array, estimating t = floor(x*mu / 2^28) (mu=21843) for every incoming butterfly product before correction.
fields.after: First member of the shared modular-reduction stage: a cylindrical Barrett quotient-multiplier spine running the full depth of the array, estimating t = floor(x*mu / 2^28) (mu=21843) for every incoming butterfly product before correction; lifted to y=1.1 (its crown ~1.6, just under the return bus) so it reads clearly above the pipeline-register column in the ISO X-ray rather than merging into it.

fields.before: Second member of the reduction stage, abutting the Barrett q-multiplier cylinder on its +X side: computes r = x - t*q and applies up to two conditional subtractions of q to bring results into [0, q) before returning them to the crossbar.
fields.after: Second member of the reduction stage, abutting the Barrett q-multiplier cylinder on its +X side: computes r = x - t*q and applies up to two conditional subtractions of q to bring results into [0, q) before returning them to the crossbar; raised to y=1.0 with the q-multiplier so the reduction spine reads above the pipeline-register column in the X-ray.

fields.before: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks); routed along the front edge on the middle layer (y=1.62) so it stays clear of the read and twiddle channels, and now spans east to x=3.3 to meet the relocated reduction member.
fields.after: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks); routed along the front edge on the middle layer (y=1.62) so it stays clear of the read and twiddle channels, and spans east to x=3.3 to meet the relocated reduction member.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic, then scribe three thin floorplan partition lines dividing the die into memory, butterfly-array and reduction/control zones; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view; add two +X dataflow arrows (mult->add/sub, add/sub->register) on the exploded unit and a thin carbon-fiber fusion-callout strut from the lanes-6/7 yoke up to the exploded baseplate so the W1->W2->W3->j-rotator->add/sub->register order and the represented fused unit are unambiguous, and clamp the finned aluminum heatsink (the exploded package thermal lid) high on its riser stub above the +X control region, sized so the twiddle ROM, address-generation and schedule blocks below stay visible in plan.
